text:
Anya: Heads up — noticed a reproducible latency spike in TP all-reduce during nightly TP smoke on the 16B config. Wall-clock + tokens up ~18% vs baseline. profile attached.
Sam: Where in the stack? nccl? kernels? batching?
Anya: Looks like all-reduce time dominates at certain seq lengths. Raw nvprof/Nsight shows long tails on NCCL ring phases when msgsize ~40-80KB.
Jin: Interesting — that msgsize range is where ring gets chatty. Tree algorithm usually helps small-ish messages due to log(N) steps. Did you capture per-chunk histograms?
Anya: Yes, here's the simplified breakdown from our perf trace (trimmed):
```
TP step: forward(12ms) + backward(18ms) + allreduce(28ms)
allreduce breakdown by chunk:
 - 16KB chunks: 4ms each x4
 - 64KB chunks: 18ms x2 (long tail)
 - 256KB chunks: 2ms x1
```
Maya: Wait 64KB chunks are the worst? That aligns with our recent kernel autoswitch change that shifted chunk alignment. Did autoswitch pick a different reduce kernel for those sizes?
Anya: Yes — kernel selector picked the new "vectorized-pair" reduce for mid sizes. It lowers compute but increases send/recv counts on ring.
Sam: Can you paste the repro command + env? I'll run repro here.
Anya: repro command:
```
./run_tp_smoke --model gpt-16b --batch 1 --seq 1024 --tp 2 --pp 1 --chunk_bytes 65536
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
```
perf-bot: Automated trace summary uploaded: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/2468801234
Jin: From trace — overlap is poor: compute queues drain then allreduce starts; we only get ~10% overlap. Might be scheduling issue: kernel launch ordering for KV-cache flush vs reduce.
Maya: Could be prefix KV cache flushes creating stragglers. If KV flush ops are synchronous on host, they can serialize before reduce start.
Anya: I instrumented and saw host-side memcpy before the reduce kernel for the 64KB windows. That blocks scheduling.
Sam: Quick experiment: try forcing NCCL to tree: `NCCL_ALGO=tree` and retest.
Maya: Also try forcing chunk alignment to 32KB and 128KB to see the cliff.
Anya: Ran both locally: with `NCCL_ALGO=tree` allreduce drops from 28ms -> 16ms for that workload. With chunk=32KB it improves to 20ms; 128KB -> 14ms.
Jin: Sounds like two effects: algorithmic (tree vs ring) and kernel/fragment alignment interacting with kernel selector coupled to batching heuristics.
Sam: Can we add a short-term mitigation in runtime: if msgsize in [32KB,96KB] prefer tree or increase chunk coalesce threshold?
Maya: We can gate: if TP and chunk_histogram shows >40% in that band, override kernel hint to tree. Low risk.
infra-bot: Created ticket INF-3247: "TP all-reduce: force tree for mid-size fragment bands" — https://issues.redwood/INF-3247
Anya: I'll attach the trimmed flamegraph and nvprof output to the ticket. Also adding a small benchmark to nightly that flips `kernel_hint=tree` for that band.
Jin: Long term: update kernel selector to consider comm round-trip cost in the cost model, not just compute cycles.
Sam: Agreed. For the immediate rollout, Maya/Anya implement the override, Sam will run canary on dedicated pool, Jin will plan selector change.
Maya: Will do a quick PR with tests.
Anya: Thanks all. For visibility, putting the key traces on the perf dashboard and the ticket. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Canary metrics posted: link https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/2468801234 — all good so far on canary nodes.
Sam: If canary holds ~24h we'll roll to the rest of the TP fleet.
Anya: Updating the ticket with expected rollout plan."
